> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> BCRP API URL is /{code}/json/{start}/{end} and fetch_series() already takes start/end, so compute max(obs_date) per series and fetch start=max_date+1 - the current skip-if-key-present logic never extends a daily series (stale for a daily source).

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Date-tail always-fetch: per series read existing bcrp.parquet max(obs_date), set start=max_date+1, end=today. No vintage feed; the daily date tail is the signal.
- `since_param`: start=<max_obs_date+1> in /{code}/json/{start}/{end} (BASE=https://estadisticas.bcrp.gob.pe/estadisticas/series/api)
- `out_paths_note`: Single file: data/clean_full/bcrp/bcrp.parquet (6 daily FX series). Needs (series_key,obs_date) dedup on append - current append has none and relies on the series-key skip to avoid dupes.
- `rate_note`: No API key. Only daily PD* series work (monthly/quarterly PN* return empty); single-series requests only (batching fails); 0.5s RATE; 3 retries linear backoff; Spanish month-name date parsing.

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/bcrp.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/bcrp.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S2 fetcher — BCRP (Banco Central de Reserva del Perú). Public domain, no key.

Layout: a single parquet under clean_full/bcrp/bcrp.parquet, schema
(series_key, obs_date, value). The public JSON API is per-series and accepts a
path-based date range /{code}/json/{start}/{end}/, so we read each series' last
obs_date from the existing file and request only newer observations, then MERGE
(dedup on series_key+obs_date, new values win on revision, never-shrink).

Only the daily PD* exchange-rate series return data via the public API; the
other PD* series (EUR/GBP/JPY here) come back as an empty-HTML stub — a 200 with
an empty <body>, BCRP's "no data for this series" sentinel — which we treat as a
legitimate EMPTY sub-unit, not a failure.

HONEST-STATUS classification (see _common.finalize):
  * A 200 whose body is JSON ([ or {)                  -> parse (data / empty).
  * A 200 that is the empty-HTML stub (empty <body>,
    no error markers) or a genuinely empty body, or a
    real 404 for one series/range                       -> EMPTY sub-unit.
  * A 200 whose body is HTML/text with CONTENT or known
    throttle/maintenance/"invalid"/"error" markers      -> TRANSIENT (retry; if
    the retry budget is exhausted, raise TransientError so the run is `partial`).
  * timeout / 5xx / 429 / connection drop               -> TRANSIENT.
A run where every requested series returned a malformed/throttle body (i.e. the
whole window came back non-JSON) surfaces as a transient `partial`, never a
silent no_change.
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/ingest_bcrp.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='bcrp'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source bcrp --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source bcrp --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('bcrp');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source bcrp
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `bcrp`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: 1 of 1 unit (`_all`). The crash aborts update() inside the SERIES loop before any merge, so 0 rows land: run 447 recorded obs=0, dur_s=0.3. It fires on the FIRST series that returns parsed rows (PD04638PD / USDPEN_mid), so sub-units 2-5 of 5 are never even requested. With the type corrected, all 5 sub-units succeed (control above).
- **blast radius**: The whole source, but only since the group_by removal: bcrp's last clean run was 2026-08-01T08:01:10Z (no_change, 31,408 obs, frontier 2026-07-30), and it has been unable to advance since. Exactly one crashing attempt is on record (2026-08-03T09:33:30Z); nothing has been attempted since, so the current damage is a 5-series daily FX store frozen at obs_date 2026-07-30 while the publisher is serving through today. No data was lost or corrupted — the crash happens before merge.merge_and_write, and the existing parquet is untouched.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Fix at the source, the way scb was, not at the consumption points. In E:\research\econfindatalibrary\updater\strategies\fetchers\bcrp.py:140-158, make _per_series_last honour its own `-> dict[str, dt.date]` annotation by adding a string branch next to the existing datetime branch:
> 
>     if isinstance(d, dt.datetime): d = d.date()
>     elif isinstance(d, str):
>         try: d = dt.date.fromisoformat(d[:10])
>         except ValueError: continue
> 
> Then the cursor seed (276) and last_db (343) keep working via their existing isinstance guards, and 327 is fixed with them. Patching only line 327 would be the third repeat of the mistake this file has now made twice: R310 chose "accept either type at each consumption point" for bcrp and MISSED one, while the same commit chose fix-at-source for scb and missed none. Add a unit test that asserts every value of _per_series_last() is a dt.date, since the defect class is "the annotation lies", not "this one line compares wrong". After the fix, force a bcrp tick — the source will stay red until it is actually re-attempted, because the transient_fail row is stale (R246).

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
